content: Prolonged use of corticosteroids can impair your body’s ability to respond effectively to physical stress. Budesonide, a corticosteroid, may suppress the typical signs of infection, potentially delaying diagnosis and treatment. It can also increase your susceptibility to infections or exacerbate existing ones. Avoid close contact with individuals who have contagious illnesses such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Inform your healthcare provider that you are using budesonide before receiving any vaccinations or immunizations. In rare cases, long-term use of this medication may temporarily slow a child’s growth. During pregnancy, budesonide should only be used if absolutely necessary, and the risks and benefits should be thoroughly discussed with your doctor. Infants born to mothers who have used corticosteroids for extended periods may develop hormonal imbalances. Additionally, this medication can pass into breast milk, so consult your healthcare provider if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of severe side effects. It is essential to maintain a comprehensive list of all medications and supplements you are taking, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter products, and herbal supplements, and share this list with your doctor and pharmacist. If your doctor has advised you to take low-dose aspirin (81–162 mg daily) to prevent heart attack or stroke, continue taking it unless instructed otherwise. In the event of an overdose, this medication can be harmful if ingested. If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. To reduce the risk of bone loss (osteoporosis) during long-term corticosteroid treatment, consider lifestyle changes such as engaging in weight-bearing exercises, ensuring adequate intake of calcium and vitamin D, quitting smoking, and limiting alcohol consumption. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from heat and open flames, as it is flammable. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your health needs.
